scope: Pinned source review of ps formatting and record-boundary behavior; no process/API query or implementation.

XNU.note: Pinned release commit identified. Direct fetch of the kern_exec.c blob at this pin was unavailable through the source browser; prior source review captured current official set_proc_name behavior separately.

findings.fixed_columns: Apple parsefmt tokenizes custom format on space, tab, comma, newline; unique ASCII header tokens must contain none of those delimiters. sizevars sets width=max(existing default width, strlen(header)). A 64-byte header therefore establishes a 64-byte minimum and complete raw-header validation detects any wider default.
findings.row_framing: The printer loop emits exactly one ASCII space between fields and one LF after each row. Use fixed byte offsets for fixed-width fields; never split on arbitrary whitespace.
findings.ucomm: ucomm prints the kernel p_comm C string using %-*s. Compare the exact raw fixed-width output to native p_comm bytes plus exact ASCII-space padding; do not trim or normalize. ucomm remains raw, so LF in p_comm breaks framing and must fail closed.
findings.args: On Apple, args uses getproclline/KERN_PROCARGS2 rather than the non-Apple fmt_argv path. The command string including fallback (p_comm) passes through strvis(VIS_TAB|VIS_NL|VIS_NOSLASH). Pinned Libc vis implementation inserts tab/newline into its forced-encode set; non-graphic controls are emitted as graphic caret/meta/octal forms. Thus args cannot inject a literal LF row delimiter. args must remain last; stdout pipe makes termwidth unlimited and the last-field path uses fputs of the transformed string.
findings.args_identity: PS documentation says arguments may be changed with setproctitle and are inherently unreliable; retain them as existing argv evidence, not as process identity.
findings.fmt_argv: The ps.c fmt_argv helper is inside #ifndef __APPLE__; it is not the macOS arguments chain examined here.

source_excerpts.name: VIS documentation: encoded range and flags
source_excerpts.excerpt:
By default, all non-graphic characters,
except space, tab, and newline are encoded.
VIS_TAB also encodes tab.
VIS_NL also encodes newline.
The default format uses caret to represent control characters.

source_excerpts.name: PS manual authority distinction
source_excerpts.excerpt:
The process can change the arguments shown with
.Xr setproctitle 3 .
Otherwise,
.Nm
makes an educated guess as to the file name and arguments given when the process was created by examining memory or the swap area.
The method is inherently somewhat unreliable and in any event a process is entitled to destroy this information.
The ucomm (accounting) keyword can, however, be depended on.
